content.text: This is a deploy request, so it is externally bound and the gate applies. Running the privacy guard over every artifact the ticket names, in one call, before hashing anything.

content.content:
privacy_guard: clean - no secret patterns across 2 path(s)
pg=0

content.text: Guard exited 0, so I build the deterministic manifest over those same two paths - sorted bytewise, hashed per file, then the manifest itself hashed - and read the ticket activity for scope drift.

input.command: python3 -c 'import hashlib,pathlib,sys; rows=[f"{hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(r).read_bytes()).hexdigest()}  {r}" for r in sorted(sys.argv[1:])]; m="\n".join(rows)+"\n"; pathlib.Path("gate-manifest.txt").write_text(m,encoding="utf-8"); print(hashlib.sha256(m.encode()).hexdigest())' ops/rollback-plan-4505.md release/scheduling-engine-4505.md > gate-digest.txt; cat gate-digest.txt

Privacy guard: clean over both paths, no secret patterns. Scope drift: committer wrote "The branch is green but I have not written a rollback path yet", so the rollback artifact hashed above is a stub and not a plan; system-watchdog reports two automation runs still in flight against the same workspace, and neither is named in this ticket's scope. Both findings are recorded here for you to weigh - I do not settle them myself.

Owner actions:
1. Approve - move the ticket to Done. The approval-mark-on-done automation then swaps pending-approval for the approved label, which every publish, send and deploy automation requires before it acts.
2. Request changes - move the ticket back to Todo and leave a comment describing what to change. That re-dispatches the producing agent automatically, which is why the assignment stays where it is.
